text: A couple has two daughters and is expecting another child. A relative claims that their next child must be a boy. Using the chromosomal basis of sex determination in humans, which response is correct?
options: The claim is correct because Y-bearing eggs become more likely after two daughters.
The claim is correct because the father's sperm now carry only Y chromosomes.
The claim is incorrect because an X-bearing egg can be fertilised by either an X-bearing or a Y-bearing sperm, independently of previous births.
The claim is incorrect because every child of the same couple must have the same sex chromosomes.
answer: C. Each egg carries an X chromosome. Fertilisation by an X-bearing sperm produces XX, while fertilisation by a Y-bearing sperm produces XY. Previous births do not determine which sperm fertilises the next egg, so the next child is not necessarily a boy.
